gatherly.tagline: Gift registries, Secret Santa and shared lists — one product for celebrations people actually plan together.
gatherly.highlight_0: Template-driven experiences with themes, public pages, roles, and atomic gift reservations.
gatherly.highlight_1: Secret Santa with exclusions, private draws, wishlists, and invite links over WhatsApp/Telegram/email.
gatherly.highlight_2: Monorepo: Next.js 16 + NestJS + Supabase Auth/Postgres + Groq AI import, live on Vercel and Render.
gatherly.problem: Event planning tools are usually either a spreadsheet, a single-purpose registry, or a heavy SaaS. Couples and friends need one calm place for gifts, Secret Santa, and shared lists — with privacy that keeps surprises intact.
gatherly.approach: Gatherly models each celebration as an experience with its own template, theme, membership roles, and public page. Gift reservations are atomic, Secret Santa draws stay private even to organizers, and AI helps import products from store links without inventing prices. Invites go out via Resend or share deep links.
gatherly.outcome: A live multi-locale product you can open today: create an experience, invite people, reserve gifts, and run Secret Santa — frontend on Vercel, API on Render, auth and data on Supabase.

neura.tagline: Chat with a CV + GitHub knowledge base — RAG, citations, hybrid search, multi-provider fallback.
neura.highlight_0: Hybrid retrieval: pgvector similarity + full-text search over ingested CV and repos.
neura.highlight_1: SSE chat with source citations and follow-up suggestions grounded in retrieved chunks.
neura.highlight_2: Groq primary with Gemini/Cerebras fallback; NestJS API on Render + Next.js on Vercel.
neura.problem: Most “AI portfolio” demos are a thin chat wrapper over a prompt. The hard part is ingesting a CV and public repos into a searchable knowledge base, retrieving the right chunks, and answering with citations that stay honest when the model fails over.
neura.approach: NeuraFolio ingests a resume PDF and GitHub repos into Neon Postgres (pgvector + FTS), serves RAG chat from a NestJS backend with hybrid retrieval and optional tool agent, and streams answers to a Next.js UI with source filters (All / CV / GitHub) and temporary visitor CV upload.
neura.outcome: A live product you can open and chat with — creator CV + GitHub by default, upload-your-own CV for a session, and a clear split between frontend (Vercel) and API/RAG (Render) on a free-tier path.

newsletter.tagline: RSS in → structured AI analysis → Postgres → a personal daily Telegram digest.
newsletter.highlight_0: Analyze once with Zod-validated LLM output — never re-score the same article.
newsletter.highlight_1: Multi-reader personalization on shared analyzed content.
newsletter.highlight_2: Production path: Vercel Cron + Supabase on a free-tier stack.
newsletter.problem: Most “AI newsletter” demos stop at a chatbot UI. The hard part is a reliable ingest → analyze → deliver pipeline that stays cheap, dedupes sources, and personalizes digests without re-running models for every reader.
newsletter.approach: InsightLoop collects RSS feeds, canonicalizes URLs, runs a structured LLM pass (Groq primary with optional failover), stores results in Postgres via Drizzle, and sends card-style Telegram digests. A Next.js dashboard covers Discover, preferences, pipeline health, and admin workflow controls.
newsletter.outcome: A portfolio-grade product you can click through live: public Discover, topic onboarding, Telegram connect, and a daily production cron — focused on orchestration, not just prompts.

pulse.tagline: Real-time Binance market terminal built for event pressure, not just “connect a WebSocket”.
pulse.highlight_0: rAF-batched stream updates to keep the UI responsive under load.
pulse.highlight_1: Local order book synced to Binance snapshot + diff sequence rules.
pulse.highlight_2: Performance Lab injects 1k–10k synthetic events/sec to prove the architecture.
pulse.problem: Many crypto demos look fine with quiet markets and fall apart when trade and depth streams spike. Re-rendering per message and naive book updates create jank and correctness bugs.
pulse.approach: Pulse Terminal uses a native WebSocket manager with reconnect/backoff, coalesces bursts on requestAnimationFrame into Zustand, virtualizes the trade feed, and keeps the local order book aligned with exchange sequence rules. Charts and depth UI stay interactive while metrics expose events/sec and UI Hz.
pulse.outcome: A dense terminal experience that demonstrates production frontend craft: streaming reliability, batching, virtualization, and measurable performance under synthetic load.
